subject: ventures/us-freelancer-tax-set-aside-calculator
professional: a CPA or enrolled agent who prepares quarterly 1040-ES estimates for sole proprietors; first checks: SE tax on 92.35% of profit with the 2026 $184,500 wage base reduced by W-2 wages, Additional Medicare Tax via Form 8959, the half-SE deduction (excluding the 0.9%), QBI base and 20%-of-taxable-income cap and the 2026 threshold/phase-in, 2026 brackets and standard deduction, and the safe harbor (lesser of 90% of current-year federal tax or 100%/110% of prior-year tax, 110% keyed to PRIOR-year AGI over $150,000), federal only.

evidence.correctness: Independent script /tmp/claude-0/audit-freelancer-tax/indep.py (no subject import; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 tables, SSA 2026 wage base, Schedule SE, Form 8959, IRC 199A, Pub 505) vs subject outputs from /tmp/claude-0/audit-freelancer-tax/observe.mjs. Pass: the worked example (single, $100k net, 5% state) SE 14,129.55, taxable 61,468.18, federal 8,235, state 4,646.76, total 27,011.31 all match; SE at $250k net 29,573.38 + Additional Medicare 277.88 match; the $400 SE floor (net 433 -> 0, 434 -> 61.32) matches. Fail: (1) the set-aside total includes the tax on W-2 wages and other income, so a $10k side gig on a $100k salary is told to set aside $16,218.62 = 162.19% of revenue, '$1,622 from every $1,000 you invoice' (the tax the gig causes is $3,048.61, 30.5%); (2) the 1040-ES '90% of this year's tax' figure and the quarter amount include the state estimate: sample says $24,310.18 vs 90% of federal tax 20,128.09; (3) the 110% prior-year safe harbor is keyed to the CURRENT year's AGI (calc.mjs:128), so prior tax 15,000 with prior AGI > $150k yields $15,000 instead of $16,500; (4) HoH 24% bracket edge 201,775 instead of 201,750 (tax at 201,775: 39,213 vs 39,215). Partial: no QBI above the threshold instead of the OBBBA $75k phase-in, disclosed, but at $250k net single the federal tax is 46,572.26 vs 36,508.77 (non-SSTB) / 38,517.46 (SSTB), and the next-$1,000 figure jumps to $9,982.16 at the cliff (net 232,000). Core SE/federal arithmetic is right; three wrong numbers a user acts on cap this at 2.
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked by running compute(): SE tax with wage base and Additional Medicare (works), half-SE deduction (works), standard deduction and 3 statuses (works), 20% QBI below threshold (works), flat state estimate (works), marginal set-aside on next $1,000 (works, but spikes at the QBI cliff), 1040-ES dates and safe harbor finding (present, wrong base), summary text and download (summaryText runs). `node --test 'ventures/us-freelancer-tax-set-aside-calculator/**/*.test.mjs'` from the repo root (README command) 29/29 pass. Served copy via `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs us-freelancer-tax-set-aside-calculator`: no placeholder origins. Live page not loaded (proxy 403 for marisstella.app). No stubs; VENTURE.yaml lists unbuilt items honestly (all-states brackets, tracker, voucher helper).
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 29 tests pass in ~75 ms. quality_mutate.py: 3 of 5 core mutants SURVIVED: Additional Medicare ignoring W-2 wages (calc.mjs:69), safe-harbor 90% -> 80% (calc.mjs:129), HoH 12% -> 15% (calc.mjs:11, no HoH test at all). Caught: the 110% multiplier and SE_FACTOR 0.9235 -> 0.9. Tests check the single worked example to the cent, but the author's own numbers, not an IRS table, and nothing covers W-2 + side gig, HoH, or the 90% path.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (151 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script. Clean pure functions, robust number parsing, two-call marginal. Defects: one `total` conflates federal and state and feeds both the set-aside share and the 1040-ES figures; the 'above the QBI line' finding fires whenever qbi is 0, including when taxable income is 0 (run with $15,000 revenue prints 'Taxable income is above the $201,750 line'); safe harbor uses current AGI as a proxy for prior AGI without saying so; currency formatter in index.html is named `cad` (copied from the Canada sibling).
evidence.claims: Checked: 'self-employment tax ... wage base and Additional Medicare' (pass, recomputed); 'Tables match ... Rev. Proc. 2025-32' (fail for HoH 24% edge 201,775 vs 201,750, Rev. Proc. Table 2 as cited in ventures/inherited-ira-10-year-withdrawal-planner/irs-table.test.mjs:11); 'the 1040-ES schedule with the safe harbor' (fail: the amount includes state tax and keys 110% to current AGI); 'the share of every invoice to set aside' (fail with W-2 wages: 162%); FAQ 'Most freelancers land between 25% and 35% of profit' (no file backs it); 'QBI limits for high earners' listed under Not decided (pass, disclosed). Disclaimer, no-warranty and verify-on-irs.gov present on page and in summary (pass).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through as an EA setting quarterly estimates: a pure 1099 single filer with no other income gets a correct federal+SE figure and sensible dates; but the client with a W-2 job (the most common side-gig case) gets a set-aside share over 100% with no withholding input, the 1040-ES amount mixes in state tax (overpays IRS, underpays the state), the prior-year safe harbor needs prior AGI which is not asked, and there is no SE health insurance / SEP deduction, MFS status or annualized-income option. Usable as a rough planning number for the simple case only.
evidence.domain: Matches practice: 92.35% factor, SS base less W-2 wages, Medicare uncapped, Form 8959 threshold reduced by wages, half-SE deduction excluding Additional Medicare, QBI = net less half-SE, capped at 20% of taxable income before QBI, 2026 single/MFJ brackets and standard deduction (16,100/32,200/24,150), $184,500 wage base, 2026 due dates. Departures: safe harbor applied to federal+state and keyed to current AGI (Pub 505 / IRC 6654(d)(1)(C) use prior-year AGI); QBI treated as a cliff at $201,750 rather than the OBBBA $75,000/$150,000 phase-in, and the 2026 $400 minimum QBI deduction is not modelled; W-2 withholding not netted from the set-aside.

defects.what: Set-aside total, % of revenue and per-$1,000 figures include the tax on W-2 wages and other income with no withholding offset: a $10k side gig on a $100k salary is told to set aside $16,218.62 (162% of revenue, $1,622 per $1,000 invoiced) when the gig causes about $3,049

1040-ES 'pay at least' amount (90% of this year's tax), the $1,000 penalty-floor test and the quarterly amount use a total that includes the state estimate; federal safe harbor is 90% of federal tax only ($24,310.18 shown vs $20,128.09 on the worked example)

110% prior-year safe harbor is triggered by the current year's AGI; IRC 6654(d)(1)(C) keys it to the preceding year's AGI, which the tool never asks, so a client whose income fell is told 100% and can be underpaid

QBI is a cliff at $201,750/$403,500 instead of the 2026 $75,000/$150,000 phase-in; at $250k net single federal tax is ~$10k too high and the 'next $1,000' figure shows $9,982 at the cliff; the 2026 $400 minimum deduction is not modelled (disclosed as not decided)
The 'Taxable income is above the $201,750 line' QBI finding fires whenever the QBI deduction is 0, including when taxable income is 0 (e.g. $15,000 revenue)
3 of 5 seeded mutants survive: no test for Additional Medicare with W-2 wages, for the 90%-of-current-year path, or for any head-of-household bracket
HoH 24% bracket ends at 201,775 instead of 201,750 (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 Table 2), up to $2 off; README says tables match Rev. Proc. 2025-32
FAQ claim 'Most freelancers land between 25% and 35% of profit' has no data or source behind it

verdict: The core arithmetic is right: an independent script reproduces the worked example to the cent (SE 14,129.55, taxable 61,468.18, federal 8,235, total 27,011.31), the wage-base cap and Additional Medicare at $250k, and the $400 SE floor. But the numbers a freelancer acts on go wrong outside the pure-1099 case: the set-aside share includes the tax on W-2 wages (162% of revenue for a $10k side gig on a $100k salary), the 1040-ES safe-harbor amount and quarterly figure include state tax, the 110% test uses current rather than prior-year AGI, QBI is a cliff instead of the 2026 phase-in, and the HoH 24% edge is $25 off. Three of five seeded mutants survive. It misses the bar on correctness, claims and verification; an EA would use it only as a rough figure for a single-source 1099 client.
